origin: 40 consecutive lines of a real Claude Code transcript. Redacted by field allowlist: every number the tool wrote is verbatim, every identifier is a stand-in, every body is replaced by the same number of placeholder lines. Nothing the parser does not read was copied.
method: Counted from the raw JSONL by a second implementation written against the log's shape, never calling internal/parser. The trace is 40 lines: each figure below is checkable by reading them.

derivations.records: 16 assistant lines carry 7 distinct message.id values. One API response is written as one line per content block, so the count of responses is the count of ids -- this is the figure v0.12 got wrong by counting lines.
derivations.sessions: every line carries the same sessionId.
derivations.input_tokens: sum of message.usage.input_tokens over the 7 distinct ids, taken once per id. Every block line of a response repeats that response's usage, so summing lines would multiply it.
derivations.output_tokens: sum of output_tokens over the 7 distinct ids.
derivations.cache_read_tokens: sum of cache_read_input_tokens over the 7 distinct ids.
derivations.cache_write_tokens: sum of cache_creation_input_tokens over the 7 distinct ids.
derivations.cache_write_1h_tokens: sum of usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens; on this trace every write bought the hour tier, so the two figures coincide and a reader billing all writes at the 5-minute rate is wrong on all of them.
derivations.reasoning_tokens: Claude Code publishes no thinking count; its depth row does not claim the signal, so the honest expectation is zero rather than a number.
derivations.lines_added: two toolUseResult entries of type 'create', bodies of 30 and 61 lines. Both carry an empty structuredPatch, which is how the source describes a creation -- a reader walking only the patch counts 0 here.
derivations.lines_removed: no toolUseResult in the window removes a line.
derivations.rework_lines: nothing is removed, so nothing undoes an earlier addition.
derivations.edits: 2 tool_use blocks named Write; the other 6 calls are Bash, Read and Agent.
derivations.tool_calls: 8 tool_use blocks across the 16 assistant lines: 3 Bash, 3 Read, 1 Agent, and the 2 Writes.
derivations.rejected: one line carries toolDenialKind. Its content block is also flagged is_error, and that is deliberately not also counted as a tool error: a human refusing a call is not the tool failing, and counting both would double one event into two friction signals.
derivations.tool_errors: no failed tool result in the window other than the denial above.
derivations.compactions: no line marks a context overflow.
derivations.skipped: every line is valid JSON and every assistant line carries a message.id.
